```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Briquet_2026_meropenem")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00372-26>
* Supplement (Tables S1-S3, Figures S1-S2): published with the article.

Briquet 2026 asks whether meropenem 2 g three times daily can be given during
the day only, so that a home-care nurse does not have to visit at night. Each
patient received the conventional schedule (doses every 8 h, "q8-8-8 h") and
then, once clinically stable, the same three doses at 6 h intervals followed by
a 12 h overnight gap ("q6-6-12 h", the OPAT-adapted schedule), all as 20 min
infusions. Unbound meropenem was measured at steady state on both schedules and
fitted with a two-compartment population model in Monolix. Monte Carlo
simulations then compared six regimens -- the two schedules with 20 min
infusions plus 3 h (conventional) and 1, 3 and 5 h (OPAT) prolonged
infusions -- by the probability of target attainment (PTA) for
f%T > MIC targets.

The model describes **unbound** concentrations (measured in serum
ultrafiltrate), so `Cc` here is the unbound concentration and the volumes are
apparent volumes referenced to it.

# Population

`r ui$population$n_subjects` non-critically ill adults hospitalised at the
Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels, between November 2019 and October
2021 contributed 246 samples (all 22 patients on the conventional schedule, 20
on the OPAT-adapted schedule), of which
`r ui$population$n_observations` were analysed. Table 1: 12 men and 10 women,
median age 61.5 years (26-82), median weight 85 kg (44-155), median BMI
26.35 kg/m^2, CKD-EPI eGFR median 102 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (64-234; 16 patients above
90 and 6 between 60 and 90). Infections were bone (15), intra-abdominal (5) and
skin and soft tissue (2), all caused by Gram-negative organisms with meropenem
MIC up to 2 mg/L. Body weight, height, sex, age, serum creatinine and eGFR were
screened as covariates and none was retained.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: two compartments, first-order elimination | -- | Results, "Population pharmacokinetic modeling" |
| `lcl` | log(11.7 L/h) | Table 2, CL |
| `lvc` | log(23.6 L) | Table 2, V1 |
| `lq` | log(1.98 L/h) | Table 2, Q |
| `lvp` | log(5.44 L) | Table 2, V2 |
| IIV form `theta_j = theta_p * exp(eta_j)` | -- | Methods equation |
| `etalcl` variance | 0.517^2 = 0.267289 | Table 2, IIV_CL (%) 51.7 (Monolix omega x 100) |
| `etalvc` variance | 0.429^2 = 0.184041 | Table 2, IIV_V1 (%) 42.9 |
| `etalcl`-`etalvc` covariance | 0.76 x 0.517 x 0.429 = 0.16856 | Table 2, Corr_V1_Cl 0.76 |
| `addSd` | 0.16 mg/L | Table 2, Additive |
| `propSd` | 0.41 | Table 2, Proportional |
| Combined residual error | -- | Results ("combined (additive plus proportional)") |
| Simulated regimens, steady state 120-144 h | -- | Methods, "Monte Carlo simulation"; Figure 2 |
| PTA reference values | -- | Supplementary Table S3 |
| Trough and fT > MIC reference values | -- | Supplementary Table S2; Results |

# Deterministic gates

```{r gate-typical}
# At eta = 0 the individual parameters must reduce to Table 2 exactly.
tv <- rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  et(amt = 2000, dur = 1 / 3, cmt = "central") |> et(0:1, cmt = "central"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(tv$cl[1], 11.7)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(tv$vc[1], 23.6)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(tv$q[1], 1.98)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(tv$vp[1], 5.44))
)

# The Table 2 omega block: SDs 0.517 / 0.429 and correlation 0.76.
om <- ui$omega
stopifnot(
  abs(sqrt(om["etalcl", "etalcl"]) - 0.517) < 1e-9,
  abs(sqrt(om["etalvc", "etalvc"]) - 0.429) < 1e-9,
  abs(om["etalcl", "etalvc"] / sqrt(om["etalcl", "etalcl"] * om["etalvc", "etalvc"]) - 0.76) < 1e-9
)
```

# Simulated regimens

All six regimens of Figure 2 and Table S3 deliver 6 g/day. Doses are given for
six days and the steady-state day 120-144 h is observed on a 5 min grid, which
lands exactly on the end of every infusion duration used (20 min, 1, 3 and 5 h).

```{r regimens}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~schedule, ~dur_h, ~label,
  "q8_20min", "q8-8-8 h", 1 / 3, "q8-8-8 h, 20 min infusion",
  "q8_3h", "q8-8-8 h", 3, "q8-8-8 h, 3 h infusion",
  "opat_20min", "q6-6-12 h", 1 / 3, "q6-6-12 h, 20 min infusion",
  "opat_1h", "q6-6-12 h", 1, "q6-6-12 h, 1 h infusion",
  "opat_3h", "q6-6-12 h", 3, "q6-6-12 h, 3 h infusion",
  "opat_5h", "q6-6-12 h", 5, "q6-6-12 h, 5 h infusion"
)
regimens$label <- factor(regimens$label, levels = regimens$label)

daily_times <- list("q8-8-8 h" = c(0, 8, 16), "q6-6-12 h" = c(0, 6, 12))
obs_grid <- seq(120, 144, by = 1 / 12)
n_per_arm <- 200

make_events <- function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  dose_t <- sort(as.numeric(outer(daily_times[[r$schedule]], seq(0, 120, by = 24), "+")))
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  doses <- expand.grid(time = dose_t, id = ids) |>
    mutate(amt = 2000, rate = 2000 / r$dur_h, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
  obs <- expand.grid(time = obs_grid, id = ids) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(regimen = r$regimen) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), make_events))
```

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
sim <- rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, cl, regimen) |>
  left_join(select(regimens, regimen, label), by = "regimen")
```

## Figure 2: steady-state concentration-time profiles

```{r figure2, fig.height = 7}
sim |>
  group_by(label, time) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(Cc),
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.025),
    hi = quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, median)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 2, linetype = "dotdash") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 8, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.05, 300)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(120, 126, 128, 132, 136, 138, 144)) +
  facet_wrap(~label, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Unbound meropenem (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Briquet 2026: median and 95% interval, 200 subjects per regimen."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

The steady-state day (120-144 h) is analysed with PKNCA for the first 100
simulated subjects of each regimen. At steady state the AUC over 24 h must
equal the daily dose (6000 mg) divided by each subject's own clearance.

```{r pknca}
nca_ids <- sim |>
  distinct(regimen, id) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  slice_head(n = 100) |>
  ungroup()
conc <- sim |>
  semi_join(nca_ids, by = c("regimen", "id")) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, time >= 120 - 24) |>
  semi_join(nca_ids, by = c("regimen", "id")) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 120, end = 144, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, cav = TRUE)
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  select(regimen, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_wide |>
  left_join(regimens, by = "regimen") |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(
    cmax = median(cmax), cmin = median(cmin),
    auc = median(auclast), cav = median(cav), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = label, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Cmin over 24 h (mg/L)" = cmin,
    "AUC 120-144 h (mg*h/L)" = auc, "Cav (mg/L)" = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median steady-state NCA by regimen (100 subjects each).")
```

```{r pknca-gate}
# Both sides use the same drawn clearance, so the difference is numerical
# (trapezoidal integration on a 5 min grid, residual approach to steady state).
cl_by_id <- sim |> distinct(regimen, id, cl)
auc_chk <- nca_wide |>
  left_join(cl_by_id, by = c("regimen", "id")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auclast / (6000 / cl) - 1))
summary(auc_chk$pct_diff)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 2
)
```

# Comparison against the published simulations

## Lowest trough (Table S2)

The lowest trough of each regimen is the concentration at 144 h: 8 h after a
conventional dose, 12 h after the evening OPAT dose.

```{r trough}
trough_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cmin,
  "q8_20min", 3.2,
  "q8_3h", 5.3,
  "opat_20min", 1.2,
  "opat_1h", 1.3,
  "opat_3h", 1.7,
  "opat_5h", 2.5
)
trough_sim <- sim |>
  filter(abs(time - 144) < 1e-6) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(cmin = median(Cc), .groups = "drop")

trough_tbl <- ncaComparisonTable(
  trough_sim |> mutate(PPTESTCD = "cmin", PPORRES = cmin) |> select(regimen, PPTESTCD, PPORRES),
  trough_ref,
  by = "regimen",
  units = c(cmin = "mg/L")
)
knitr::kable(trough_tbl, caption = "Median lowest trough versus Table S2 (paper: median of 1,000 simulated subjects).")

trough_chk <- left_join(trough_sim, trough_ref, by = "regimen", suffix = c("_sim", "_ref")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (cmin_sim / cmin_ref - 1))
trough_chk
# Each simulated median of 200 log-spread troughs carries roughly 10% Monte
# Carlo error, so the gate is on the centre across regimens and on a bound
# several SEs wide per regimen; a transcription error in CL or V1 moves every
# trough by far more. Realised on this cohort: median -6.1%, largest |diff|
# 19.1% (OPAT 3 h); a 5,000-subject run gave 3.20 / 5.16 / 1.15 / 1.27 / 1.68 /
# 2.37 mg/L against the printed 3.2 / 5.3 / 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.7 / 2.5.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(trough_chk$pct_diff)) < 15,
  max(abs(trough_chk$pct_diff)) < 40
)
```

The ordering the paper draws its main caution from is reproduced: the overnight
trough of every OPAT regimen sits below the conventional 20 min regimen's
trough, and lengthening the OPAT infusion raises it.

## Probability of target attainment (Table S3, Figure 3)

f%T > MIC is the fraction of the steady-state day (120-144 h) for which the
unbound concentration exceeds the MIC; a subject attains a target of X% when
that fraction is at least X%.

```{r pta-sim}
targets <- c(30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 100)
mics <- c(0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)
ft <- sim |>
  filter(time < 144) |>
  select(regimen, id, Cc) |>
  cross_join(tibble(mic = mics)) |>
  group_by(regimen, id, mic) |>
  summarise(ft = 100 * mean(Cc > mic), .groups = "drop")
pta_sim <- ft |>
  cross_join(tibble(target = targets)) |>
  group_by(regimen, mic, target) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(ft >= target - 1e-9), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r pta-ref}
# Supplementary Table S3, one block per target. Columns in regimen order:
# q8 20 min, q8 3 h, OPAT 20 min, OPAT 1 h, OPAT 3 h, OPAT 5 h.
s3 <- function(target, mic, ...) {
  v <- c(...)
  tibble(target = target, mic = mic, regimen = regimens$regimen, pta_ref = v)
}

```

```{r pta-gate}
pta_cmp |>
  group_by(target) |>
  summarise(
    median_abs_diff = median(abs(diff)),
    max_abs_diff = max(abs(diff)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Target (% fT > MIC)" = target,
    "Median |PTA difference| (points)" = median_abs_diff,
    "Max |PTA difference| (points)" = max_abs_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated minus Table S3 PTA, all 6 regimens x MICs.")

# 200 subjects per arm against the paper's 1,000: a mid-range PTA carries a
# Monte Carlo SE near 3 points here, so the gate is on the centre and on a
# robust quantile of the 234 cells, not on the worst cell. A mis-transcribed
# clearance or volume shifts whole MIC columns by tens of points. Realised on
# this cohort: median 1.5 points, 90th percentile 6.3 points.
c(median = median(abs(pta_cmp$diff)), q90 = unname(quantile(abs(pta_cmp$diff), 0.9)))
stopifnot(
  median(abs(pta_cmp$diff)) < 3,
  quantile(abs(pta_cmp$diff), 0.9) < 10
)
```

The 100% fT > MIC block is the most sensitive to the size of the
inter-individual variability (it is set by the lower tail of the overnight
trough), and it is reproduced closely. This also supports reading the Table 2
"IIV (%)" entries as Monolix omega values x 100 (see below).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** Table 2 prints "IIV_CL (%) 51.7" and "IIV_V1 (%) 42.9".
  Monolix reports random effects as omega, the standard deviation of the
  log-scale random effect, so these are read as omega = 0.517 and 0.429 and
  squared for `ini()`. The alternative reading, a log-normal CV% (omega =
  0.487 and 0.411), narrows the distribution slightly. In a 5,000-subject
  check against Table S3 the omega reading reproduced the 100% fT > MIC row at
  1 mg/L for the conventional 20 min regimen as 84.8% (paper 84.8%) against
  87.7% for the CV reading, and was closer for the 40% fT > MIC row at 8 mg/L
  across regimens. Typical-value predictions do not depend on this choice.
* **Combined residual error form.** The paper says "combined (additive plus
  proportional)" without the Monolix variant. Monolix's default `combined1`
  (`y = f + (a + b f) e`) is encoded. The residual error does not enter any of
  the comparisons above, which use the individual prediction `Cc`, as the
  paper's simulated concentrations appear to.
* **Simulation design.** The paper used Simulx with 1,000 subjects per
  regimen; this article uses 200, so the PTA comparison carries a larger Monte
  Carlo error. f%T > MIC is computed over the steady-state day 120-144 h
  (Methods), on a 5 min grid.
* **Table S2 versus Results text.** The ranges quoted for the overnight OPAT
  troughs differ between the Results text (e.g. 1.2 [0.01-13] mg/L for the
  20 min infusion) and Table S2 (1.2 [0.1-11] mg/L); the medians agree, and
  only the medians are compared here.
* **Figure 3 versus Table S3.** The Figure 3 legend lists five regimens (no
  5 h OPAT infusion) while Table S3 tabulates six; all six are simulated here.
* **Unbound concentrations.** All data and simulations in the paper are unbound
  meropenem; no protein-binding correction is applied or needed to compare
  `Cc` with an MIC.
* **No covariates.** None was retained in the final model, so the model applies
  to the studied population only: non-critically ill adults with eGFR of
  roughly 60-230 mL/min/1.73 m^2. It should not be used for renal impairment,
  where meropenem clearance falls.
* A literature check for errata (Crossref, 2026-11-13) found none.
